summary: In Currier B paragraph text, the share of certain words ending in EVA m is at least ten times greater at line ends than in line interiors and exceeds the within-line permutation null.
Test Latin substitution on Takahashi with glyph order reversed within words at the published noisy-control search budget.
Test the fixed glyph-substitution layer of Caspari and Faccini's proposed Italian shorthand key.
Among nine public-practice Latin substitution searches, Takahashi with reversed word order gave the highest compression savings (−11.122% versus −11.442% for the previous key), at the per-view budget
Catalogue Rozanova and Temerev's controlled tests of Voynich glyphs, tokens and separators.

Catalogue Zhang and Sheng's calibrated comparisons of Voynich text, cipher controls and copying models.

For scribe 1, a mixture led by a trigram glyph model with page-local copying, line-position vocabulary and two prefix templates beats the bag of words by about 0.33 bits per word on the practice split
Catalogue Layfield and Davis's latent semantic analysis of text similarity and transitions.

Dispatch: the fact-attack format could not test positional facts; a line-aware fix and three test-power fixes are in review.
Proposes a concrete J step: get the search out of the ch/sch trap so it cracks the German substitution control, where the true key passes at 2% noise but the search fails even clean.

On public pages one fixed procedure (an order-4 glyph chain that starts afresh at each line) matches within-line edge dependence, its collapse at line breaks and the word-length distribution together;
Test German substitution with the key found by the pinned search plus whole-homophone-group swaps, the move that cracks the German control at 2% noise.
Test Vlegels’s published Italian token map and deterministic prefix rules.
